# Softanza Radar

> What changed in AI and the tech field this week, and what it means for what we build in Softanza. Softanza Radar reads the week's papers, releases, security findings and practices at their source, judges each one from Softanza's point of view, and tells us, the Softanza team, what it means for us and what we should do about it: a check to run, a lesson to learn, or work proposed to the part it concerns.

Every file below is plain data or plain text. The two feed files are signed with SSH (Ed25519, namespace radar-feed, signer feed@radar): check a signature before trusting a feed.

## Feeds
- [Feed index](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/feed/index.json): every entry as data; its signature is feed/index.json.sig, its contract docs/FEED.md
- [JSON Feed 1.1](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/feed/feed.json): the same entries for feed readers; signature feed/feed.json.sig
- [Signer key](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/keys/allowed_signers): the public key both signatures are checked against
- [Configuration](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/app/config.json): the project, its readers, its stances and where its map is
- [Map](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/map/estate.json): the project's layers, parts, domains and concerns

## Signals, newest first
- [NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B: a 4 GB model for local agents; Softanza adds its Gemma 4 family and takes it to the model court](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-11-nemotron-bolt-e4b.md): advice, release, adopt, 2026-11-11. On October 23, 2026 NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, a small language model post-trained by reinforcement learning from Google's Gemma 4 E4B for multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding. It has 8 billion parameters, 4 billion of them effective, a 64K-token context, and ships as a 4 GB Q4_K_M GGUF file for llama.cpp with a companion DFlash drafter for speculative decoding. Its weights, training data and recipes are published under the OpenMDW-1.1 licence, and NVIDIA's own benchmark table puts it ahead of Gemma 4 E4B on most of 21 agent and instruction tests.
- [NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B finds pages by text or by image in 34 languages; Softanza measures it on Arabic and French retrieval](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-11-nemotron-embed-1b.md): advice, release, watch, 2026-11-11. On October 20, 2026 NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B, an embedding model that turns a query, a passage or the image of a document page into one vector, for retrieval across text, tables, charts and infographics. NVIDIA evaluated text retrieval in 34 languages, Arabic, French and Persian among them, and image retrieval in 18; its vectors can be cut to 1024 or 512 dimensions and stay usable once normalised. It is published under OpenMDW-1.1, with an NVFP4 variant for recent NVIDIA GPUs.
- [NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Parse reads a page into text, tables and layout with 0.63 billion parameters; Softanza's OCR court hears it](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-11-nemotron-parse.md): advice, release, learn, 2026-11-11. On October 17, 2026 NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a 0.631-billion-parameter model that turns a page image into text, tables, chart data, reading order, semantic classes and bounding boxes, exported as Markdown, HTML or JSON. NVIDIA reports 75.20 on the ParseBench benchmark in its three-pass mode, the best of the systems it compares, and multilingual OCR evaluated over 163 language and script entries. On November 4 it added a native 89.3-million-parameter DFlash2 drafter for speculative decoding; the model is published under OpenMDW-1.1.
- [NVIDIA ships a small drafter with each new model and speeds up llama.cpp; Softanza takes the algorithm into its own decoder](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-11-speculative-decoding-dflash.md): advice, practice, correct, 2026-11-11. On September 3, 2026 NVIDIA said its work with the llama.cpp and vLLM communities gives up to 1.9 times higher local throughput on a GeForce RTX 5090, from GPU kernel work, better speculative decoding and faster prefill. Since then its new models ship with a small DFlash drafter, which llama.cpp's official server runs, and its open-source C++ runtime TensorRT Edge-LLM (0.11.1, October 28) added the Bolt E4B drafter and TensorRT for RTX on Windows. Most of the speed comes from CUDA code for NVIDIA's newest GPUs; the speculative-decoding algorithm itself is portable.
- [Radar runs for any project: one file says what its agent learns and watches](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-09-lookout-for-any-project.md): info, feature, adopt, 2026-11-09. Radar now reads everything that belongs to its project from one file, radar.yaml: the project, the watch, its readers, its map, and what the watching agent learns before each survey. The feed, the site with its trends, and the bar take their names and texts from it, and version 1.1.0 of the bar reads any watch's feed with the key the page gives it.
- [A coding agent's "don't ask again" writes secrets into a file that gets published](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-agent-approvals-leak-secrets.md): action, security, defend, 2026-11-08. Apiiro reports that when a Claude Code user approves a command with "Yes, and don't ask again", the exact command, including any password or key typed into it, is saved as a permission rule in .claude/settings.local.json inside the project. The file is kept out of git only by the developer's global ignore list, not by the repository's own .gitignore, and Apiiro counted 1,122 public copies on GitHub holding a real secret, out of 104,185.
- [Radar's feed is signed: check it came from this repository unchanged](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-feed-signing.md): info, feature, adopt, 2026-11-08. Radar publishes an SSH signature beside each feed file, feed/index.json.sig and feed/feed.json.sig, made with one Ed25519 key kept for this purpose by Radar's maintainer. Any reader with OpenSSH can check a feed with ssh-keygen against the public key and the namespace radar-feed. The change adds files and adds nothing to the feed itself, so the feed stays at version 1; docs/FEED.md gives the key, its fingerprint and the command.
- [GitHub will block pull_request_target in public repositories from December 2](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-github-blocks-pull-request-target.md): info, practice, adopt, 2026-11-08. GitHub announced on November 2, 2026 that from December 2, 2026, GitHub Actions blocks pull_request_target events by default in every public repository unless an Actions event policy allows them. Enforcement is tried in two windows, November 9 and November 16, 16:00 to 18:00 UTC. Private and internal repositories are not affected.
- [Code repaired by a model after an API change can pass its checks and still be wrong](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-llm-repairs-pass-wrong.md): advice, paper, adopt, 2026-11-08. A study submitted on November 5, 2026 looks at code that models repair after documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite. Repairs that run cleanly can still give wrong answers: a gate built on typical inputs let 41% of the wrong repairs through, and adding one input written from the release note cut that to 6.5%. The expected outputs came from the old program on the old runtime.
- [Radar opens: a public watch on AI, read from Softanza's point of view](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-lookout-opens.md): info, idea, adopt, 2026-11-08. Softanza opened Radar, a public repository that reads developments in AI at their source and judges each one against what Softanza builds. Every entry is written twice in one file, as a page for people and as data for programs, and a feed is generated from the data.
- [Two MCP clients let a malicious server obtain a token meant for another server](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-mcp-oauth-resource-check.md): advice, security, defend, 2026-11-08. Two advisories published on November 5, 2026 describe the same flaw in two MCP clients, the Go SDK mcp-go before 1.2.1 and the ChatCLI agent before 1.215.2: the client took the resource named in a server's protected resource metadata without checking that it matched the server it had connected to. A malicious MCP server could name another server on the same authorization server, have the user sign in, and replay the token it received.
- [SPILLWAY: an agent may act only on targets that came from a trusted, typed field](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-spillway-target-admission.md): advice, paper, learn, 2026-11-08. A paper submitted on November 4, 2026 proposes a defence for tool-using agents against prompt injection that does not rely on a model: a call with side effects is admitted only if every target it names that is not in the user's request was returned in a typed identity field, such as an email address or a channel, by a read-only tool. A rule-based sanitizer removes instruction-like text, and a local model reviews only the calls the rule refused. The authors report no successful in-scope attack across twelve benchmark settings.
- [A prompt library ran any function a template named: tools must come from a registry](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-tool-paths-from-prompts-run-code.md): advice, security, learn, 2026-11-08. The Python prompt library banks, up to version 2.4.2, read a tool's import path from the text of a prompt template and imported and called whatever it named when the model asked for that tool (CVE-2026-61536, high). Whoever could write a template, in a shared registry or a fetched prompt, could run code in the application. Version 2.4.3 resolves tools only from a registry filled at render time.
- [Zig 0.17.1 fixes the blockers of 0.17.0; Softanza measures the move from 0.15.2](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/items/2026/2026-11-08-zig-0-17-1.md): advice, release, watch, 2026-11-08. Zig 0.17.1 is a bug-fix release that addresses more than 57 issues reported after 0.17.0, chiefly regressions and upgrade blockers; the project says most users who could not move to 0.17.0 should be able to move to 0.17.1. Its news page dates it November 3, 2026 and its download page November 2.

## About
- [Why](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/docs/WHY.md): what the watch answers and the requirements behind it
- [Method](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/docs/METHOD.md): how a signal is read, judged, written and published
- [Feed contract](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/docs/FEED.md): every field of an entry, and how a program shows a notice
- [Run your own](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/docs/ADOPT.md): the same watch for another project, from one file
- [MCP server](https://mayouni.github.io/stzradar/docs/MCP.md): ask the radar from any MCP agent (tools/mcp.haro, read-only, checks the signature first)
